does: Scrubs the shells of mussels and pulls off the tuft of fibres at the hinge, which is called the beard, so that nothing gritty reaches the pot. Mussels are cleaned just before they are cooked.

intro.what: Shells are scrubbed and the fibrous beards removed before mussels enter the pot.
intro.why: Careful cleaning separates grit from the shellfish and shows why direction matters when removing an attached fibre.

how: Tip the mussels into a bowl of cold water and lift them out by the handful, leaving the grit in the bottom of the bowl.
Tap any open shell on the side of the bowl. Leave out any that stays open.
Scrape off barnacles and dirt with the back of a knife.
Take the tuft of fibres at the hinge between a thumb and the knife blade and pull it firmly towards the hinge end until it comes away.
Rinse once more and keep the mussels cold until they go into the pot.

cues.text: The shells are closed and clean, with no tufts left sticking out.
They smell fresh, of clean sea water.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the mussels to soak for a long time in fresh water, which weakens them.
mistakes.fix: Rinse them quickly in cold water and cook them soon after.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling the beard the wrong way, towards the point of the shell, which can tear the mussel.

quiz.question: What is the cleaning step intended to remove?
choices: Shell grit and the attached fibrous beard.
The hinge that joins the shell.
quiz.because: Cleaning removes exterior debris and fibres before they reach the pot.

quiz.question: In which direction should the beard be pulled?
choices: Straight away while twisting the shell apart.
quiz.because: Pulling toward the hinge avoids the tearing associated with pulling the other way.

quiz.question: What visual cue shows beard removal?
choices: The beard remains stretched along the shell.
Fibres still hang below a polished shell.
No fibrous tuft projects from the hinge area.
quiz.because: Looking at the hinge area checks whether the attached tuft remains.

quiz.question: Grit from the bowl ends up back with the mussels. What should change?
choices: Lift the mussels out and leave the settled grit behind.
Pour the whole bowl through the mussels again.
Stir the sediment up before lifting them.
quiz.because: Lifting the mussels away separates them from debris that has settled below.

variant_of.differs: Clams are left to stand in salted water so that they give up their sand. Mussels hold little sand, so they are scrubbed, bearded and cooked soon after, and are never left to stand.
